input.title: Lifecycle Systems — Ownership Reference
input.body:
## Function Lead
Approved function lead: **the user** (charter approved 1-27-25). Retains disputed semantics, cross-surface consequences, customer corrections, incident stops, state-changing sends, ambiguous/exception-heavy cases, and executive-facing claims across all lanes.

## Standing Lanes

**Measurement — Owen**
Owns the routine exception ledger and operating explanation (unique-decision denominator, hold dispositions). Independently closes routine source-completeness review across the four board-evidence lanes (Helio Start, Expansion Assist, pricing-page path quality, CS auto-nudge controls) when all required fields are present, definitions are unchanged, owners have certified, and there's no cross-surface discrepancy. Escalates to the user on any missing field or disputed interpretation. Does not have authority over board readiness, causal claims, revenue/forecast treatment, or executive language.

**Lifecycle Governance — Ines**
Owns routine, non-state-changing lifecycle sends (3/week cap, 24hr audit, fail-closed). Independently closes routine CS auto-nudge messaging-state reviews and owns routine operator guidance for that lane when governed fields are stable/consistent and no customer-correction, incident-stop, state-change, ambiguity, exception, or disputed-semantics condition applies. May revise connector-specific instructional wording in the Helio Start authority checklist (wording only — not trigger conditions or governed-state meanings). No engineering release-control access.

**Engineering Reliability — Daniela**
Retains engineering release and rollback control across all lanes. Must approve any connector-detection logic or release-behavior change.

## Notes for New Collaborators
- These are bounded, routine-only delegations layered on top of the original charter — not a transfer of overall ownership.
- Any disputed, ambiguous, exception-heavy, or executive-facing matter escalates to the user regardless of lane.
- For full history and decision dates, see the Lifecycle Systems role reference and arc records.

## Purpose

Reusable working template for assembling and certifying evidence ahead of each quarterly board packet. One row per evidence item, grouped into four lanes. No row may be marked **Ready** until it clears the gate at the bottom.

## Lane structure

| Lane | Scope | Typical owner |
|---|---|---|
| 1 — Lifecycle Systems | Send caps, exception handling, closure mechanics, snapshot certification | Owen |
| 2 — CS / Customer-Facing Systems | Auto-nudge, readiness notes, handoff cards, CS coordination | Ines |
| 3 — Growth Initiatives | Helio Start, pricing tests, Expansion Assist, paid-source reconciliation | Growth/Priya |
| 4 — Cross-Cutting / Admin | Access reviews, vendor renewals, contractor capacity, anything spanning lanes 1–3 | Rotating |

Add rows freely within a lane; do not merge lanes to save space — mixed-lane rows are what caused prior rework (see [[feedback_aggregate_crosstab_required_for_causal_claims]]).

## Row template

Copy this block per evidence item:

```
Lane:                (1 / 2 / 3 / 4)
Evidence item:        (short name)
Claim being made:     (exact sentence as it will appear in the board packet)
Data source:          (system/table/export, as-of date)
Denominator:          (explicit N, not a lone %)
Remaining/unresolved: (count still open, or "0")
Status:               (Not Started / In Progress / Complete–Unverified / Verified–Ready)
Owner:                 
Last updated:         
Verification note:    (who checked it, against what, when)
```

## Status definitions (always show all four — never collapse to one percentage)

- **Not Started** — no data pulled yet.
- **In Progress** — data pulled, not reconciled or reviewed.
- **Complete–Unverified** — data reconciled but not independently checked or sourced-confirmed (e.g., still an internal draft — see [[feedback_ines_evidence_lock_overclaim_sep2025]]).
- **Verified–Ready** — cleared the gate below.

## Readiness gate (all must be true before a row can be set to Verified–Ready)

1. **Denominator + remaining shown**, not a single percentage or early-maturity claim ([[feedback_interim_maturity_no_early_call.md]], [[feedback_quarter_close_no_victory_lap_framing]]).
2. **Source is live/certified data, not an internal draft** ([[feedback_ines_evidence_lock_overclaim_sep2025]]).
3. **Claim wording matches approved framing for that item's domain** — e.g. no revenue language on MTD/MRR snapshots ([[feedback_riley_mrr_snapshot_framing]]), no "blocked" framing on learning-stage items ([[feedback_framing_for_tomas_reviews]]), eligibility ≠ exposure distinctions preserved ([[feedback_expansion_assist_eligibility_vs_exposure]]).
4. **No cross-lane blending** — causal or comparative claims only within a single defined cohort/breakdown ([[feedback_aggregate_crosstab_required_for_causal_claims]]).
5. **Named sign-off** — lane owner has confirmed the row in writing (name + date in Verification note), separate from whoever pulled the data.
6. **No pending-authority items presented as decided** — anything still awaiting approval stays at Complete–Unverified regardless of data quality ([[project_ines_helio_start_preflight_block_pending_authority]]).

If any of 1–6 fails, the row stays at **Complete–Unverified** and is excluded from the board-ready roll-up. Do not average or round up lane status — a lane is only Ready when every row in it is Ready.

## Roll-up rule

Report lane status as a count (e.g., "6 of 8 rows Verified–Ready"), never as a single aggregate percentage across lanes. This mirrors the day-90 status table rule ([[feedback_day90_status_table_framing]]).

input.title: Expansion nudge evidence trajectory — 2028 planning
input.body:
## Expansion nudge evidence trajectory — 2028 planning

**Experiment:** EXP-2023-05-expansion-nudge (flag `expansion_nudge_60d_v1`)

### Design (locked 2023-05-21)
- Scope: retained mid-seg only, 75–200 seats, v2 accounts.
- Mechanism: in-product prompt at day 60.
- Target: at least +$8 expansion MRR/account vs. control.
- Rollout: started conservative at 25% (deliberately avoided 50% to prevent a week of arguing over noise), with a 2-week window contingent on the power math holding.
- Went live 2023-05-23. Ownership: user owned the run, Owen ran weekly cuts, Ines owned nudge copy.

### First weekly observation (2023-06-01)
- +$4 expansion MRR/account vs. control, n=92.
- **Early sample limitation:** n=92 was explicitly treated as unreadable despite being the first "cross" moment — no directional claim was drawn from it.
- **Decision after this read:** logged and moved on with no reaction; plan set to wait **two more weeks of data** before drawing any real read, per the standing stabilization-cohort discipline (don't ship or react to a first significance/first-cross moment).

### Subsequent reads
- 2023-06-08: +$5/acct, still below the +$8 bar; lift concentrated in high-integration-depth, multi-admin accounts (usage-readiness hypothesis emerges).
- 2023-06-22: +$6.10/acct aggregate (n=372); depth split confirms — high-depth slice (n=118) +$13.20/acct, low-depth slice (n=142) +$0.60/acct. Owen: "behavior-gated, not day-60-gated." Widening declined.
- 2023-06-29 (final mature read): n=392, aggregate +$6.20/acct, p=0.16 (not significant), still below +$8 bar. Depth split held a third consecutive time.

### Final conclusion (closed 2023-06-29)
- **Status: inconclusive.** Aggregate lift settled below the +$8 MRR/account bar and was not statistically significant.
- **Final rollout boundary:** no blanket rollout. The flag was not widened off the strong high-depth subgroup (a post-hoc slice, not a pre-registered criterion) and stayed capped at 25% before being fully stood down to 0% (rolled back, 2023-07-20) to remove any residual exposure that could be mistaken for rollout momentum.
- **Learning carryforward:** the reproducible high-depth/multi-admin pattern seeded the behavior-based "Expansion Assist" follow-on track — a separately scoped, eligibility-gated design effort, not a reopening or scaling of this experiment.

tests.answer:
Based on the 2024-03-04 approval and the 2024-03-18 GA launch, here's the routing reference for Helio Start's public self-serve intake:

## Helio Start — Public Intake Routing Reference
*(rules approved 2024-03-04, live since 2024-03-18 GA)*

**Scope:** Public pricing-page self-serve path, under-50-seat accounts only. Paid acquisition and pipeline-forecast language are explicitly out of scope for this launch — don't fold them into routing descriptions.

### Eligibility gate (all required for self-serve admission)
1. Admin proof
2. Deployment simplicity
3. First-week integration fit
4. Current entitlement state
5. Supported billing conditions

*Exception:* domain mismatches can still qualify with corroborating evidence (same pattern validated at the readiness gate) — not an automatic disqualifier.

### Route-out categories (sent to assisted path, not self-serve)
- Agency/consultant identities
- Manual billing
- Imports / data migrations
- Unsupported permission needs

### Intake mechanics (structured form, shipped 3-28-24)
Applicant selects one of: supported first integration / import-migration needs / ownership-permission help / agency-consultant status. No free-text box (privacy-approved change). CS confirmed these choices map correctly to four outcomes:

| Choice | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Supported first integration + all 5 eligibility conditions met | **Eligible** → self-serve |
| Ownership/permission unclear | **Pending** → holds until resolved, not admitted |
| Import/migration, or eligible-but-flagged-for-help | **Assisted** → routed to CS |
| Agency/consultant, unsupported permissions, or manual billing | **Ineligible** for self-serve |

Live smoke test (3-18-24) confirmed all four branches produce correct outcomes end to end.

**Note:** this reflects only what was approved at the March 2024 launch. A sixth gate (external-authority confirmation) was added later, in December 2024, as a separate addition — not part of the March rules — so I left it out per your scope. Let me know if you want it folded in too.

input.title: EXP-2023-02-pricing-page — Historical Midpoint vs. Final Read (Reviewer Note)
input.body:
**Purpose:** This note exists to prevent readers from mistaking the first-week interim checkpoint for the final, powered result on EXP-2023-02-pricing-page. The two reads point in the same direction but differ in confidence, and only one of them was ever treated as a decision-grade result at the time.

## Archived final result (system of record)

- Metric: signup-to-paid conversion
- Uplift: **-1.8 pts**
- p-value: **0.03**

This is the only result stored in the experiment archive and is the powered, 2-week read. It is the number that should be cited as "the result" of this experiment.

---

## 1. First-week checkpoint (2023-03-17) — interim, not a verdict

- Treatment showed **~-0.6 pts** vs. control on signup-to-paid conversion.
- The confidence interval **still crossed zero** — not statistically distinguishable from no effect.
- Explicit decision at this point: **no action taken.** The flag (`pricing_page_2023q2_rev`) was left running at 50% exposure. This was a monitoring read, not a call to ship, hold, or roll back.
- Framing used internally at the time: "a read, not a verdict." The CRO stakeholder (Marcus Vail) was already anxious about early movement, but the team explicitly declined to react to it.

**Uncertainty at this stage:** small sample, wide CI, direction only weakly suggestive. Not sufficient on its own to support any conclusion about the pricing-page change.

## 2. Powered two-week read (2023-03-20) — the decision-grade result

- Treatment: **-1.8 pts** on signup-to-paid conversion, **p = 0.03**.
- Independently reproduced: Owen's cohort cut matched a separate rerun, ruling out a query/tooling bug.
- Status flipped from "running" to "underperforming."
- **Decision:** flag `pricing_page_2023q2_rev` rolled back to 0% the same day. Confirmed off in PostHog 2023-03-22.
- Framing: "redesign not tweak" — no partial copy/CTA salvage attempted.

## Known confound affecting the final read

An unrelated signup-form layout change merged 2023-03-02, inside the same measurement window as this test (launched 2023-03-07). This was flagged as a risk before launch and never resolved. The -1.8pt/p=0.03 result is therefore **not a clean isolated read of the pricing-page change alone** — the postmortem (2023-03-28) records this explicitly rather than presenting the number as a clean causal result.

---

## Why this separation matters for reviewers

| | First-week checkpoint (03-17) | Powered read (03-20) |
|---|---|---|
| Uplift | ~-0.6 pts | -1.8 pts |
| Statistical confidence | CI crosses zero | p = 0.03 |
| Action taken | None — flag left running | Rollback to 0% |
| Status at the time | "read, not verdict" | "underperforming," decision made |
| Confound caveat | N/A (too early to matter) | Applies — Mar 2 signup-form change in window |

Do not cite the -0.6pt interim number as the experiment's result, and do not treat the -1.8pt/p=0.03 number as a clean, confound-free causal estimate — it is the correct decision-grade read that drove the rollback, but it carries the signup-form confound caveat noted in the postmortem.

input.title: Expansion Assist Q4 second-cohort candidate audit
input.body:
## Scope

Candidate-audit worksheet for the historical Expansion Assist second cohort (cohort 2, Q4 2024 bounded cohort), evaluated against the cohort's applicable usage-ceiling recency rule as of an eligibility-check date of **October 15, 2024**.

This worksheet checks a single gate — the usage-ceiling event recency requirement. It is not an exposure record and does not imply the prompt was shown, timestamped, or that any outcome-tracking window has started. Eligibility under this rule is a point-in-time gate status, not an event; a candidate passing here could still be suppressed, held, or otherwise ineligible under other gates (active CS adoption/renewal work, admin-state currency, etc.) not evaluated in this worksheet.

tests.request: Review the inbox folder for recent payroll or benefits emails, then create a 2027 HSA tax reconciliation. input.title: 2027 HSA Tax Reconciliation
input.body:
**Source note:** Inbox, archive, and trash contained zero payroll/benefits emails as of 2028-01-01. This reconciliation is built entirely from prior confirmed tracking notes (payroll portal confirmations through 2027-12-15), not from a W-2 or HSA custodian Form 5498. No W-2/5498 has been reviewed — treat the totals below as payroll-portal-confirmed, not yet cross-checked against tax forms.

## Expected employee funding (payroll election)
- Election: $125/paycheck × 24 paychecks (biweekly, full 2027 plan year)
- Expected total: **$3,000**
- Note: a midyear election-change window closed 7-12-27 with no change submitted, so the $125/paycheck rate ran unchanged for the full year — this was a decision by inaction, not an oversight.

## Employer deposit schedule and eligibility condition
- Schedule: $225/quarter, 4 deposits/year = $900/yr target
- **Exact eligibility condition:** each $225 deposit is contingent on the employee being HSA-eligible *on that specific deposit date* — defined as: enrolled in the HDHP, not enrolled in Medicare, no other non-HDHP coverage, no general-purpose FSA/HRA, and not claimable as another person's dependent. A mid-year loss of eligibility would prorate that deposit down, not just stop future ones.
- Confirmed deposit dates: Q1 = 2-5-27, Q2 = 5-7-27, Q4 = 10-15-27 (confirmed as the fourth and final deposit). **Q3 exact date is not in the record — unknown, not assumed to be $0 or a fixed date.**

## Confirmed amounts (as of final 2027-12-15 check)
| Source | Confirmed total |
|---|---|
| Employee payroll contributions (24 × $125) | $3,000 |
| Employer quarterly deposits (4 × $225) | $900 |
| **Combined 2027 HSA funding** | **$3,900** |

Both lines were confirmed posted with no remaining pending or duplicate entries as of the 2027-12-15 closeout check.

## Supported variance
- **Duplicate employer deposit (resolved):** A duplicate $225 employer deposit dated 5-7-27 posted in error. Confirmed employer total through 5-7-27 was actually $450 (2 of 4 quarterly deposits), not $675. Payroll/custodian issued a correcting negative $225 entry; portal reflected the fix by 5-14-27, with the two legitimate deposits (2-5-27, 5-7-27) intact. This variance is fully resolved and already reflected in the $900 final employer total above — it should not be counted again as an adjustment.

## Unknowns (not treated as zero)
- **Q3 2027 employer deposit exact date:** not recorded — needed to fully itemize the quarterly schedule.
- **W-2 Box 12 Code W amount:** not yet checked against a W-2. Employer contributions plus employee payroll (pre-tax) contributions are typically combined in Box 12 W; that figure has not been verified against the $900/$3,000 figures here.
- **HSA custodian Form 5498-SA:** not reviewed. This is the authoritative document for total contributions reported to the IRS and could reveal timing differences (e.g., a contribution posted by the custodian in a different calendar period than payroll shows).
- **Continuous HSA eligibility for the full year:** confirmed as of the 2027-10-30-26-election review and again through the 5-13-27 correction, but no explicit year-end (12-31-27) reconfirmation of uninterrupted eligibility is in the record.
- **$4,500 figure used as "employee-only contribution ceiling":** this was the planning reference used in prior tracking, not something confirmed against the actual IRS annual HSA limit for the applicable coverage tier — worth verifying against the actual limit before treating $3,900 as "under the cap" for tax-filing purposes.

Because no new payroll/benefits emails exist in the inbox for this cycle, none of the above unknowns can be resolved right now — they're listed as open items rather than assumed to be $0 or immaterial.

tests.request: Create a focused, reusable review sheet for the new Expansion Assist lifecycle and in-product prompts. Center it on whether each message has a valid current-state reason to act rather than broad style guidance. Then DM Ines and ask her to apply the sheet to the draft set.

input.title: Expansion Assist Lifecycle & In-Product Prompt Review Sheet
input.body:
## Purpose

For each draft lifecycle message or in-product prompt in the Expansion Assist set, answer one question first: **does this account currently have a valid, present-tense reason to receive this message?** Style, tone, and copy polish are out of scope for this sheet — route those separately. This sheet only certifies that the message matches current account state at the moment it would send.

A message fails this review if it would still go out (or still read as accurate) after the account's state has moved on, even if the copy itself is well-written.

## Per-message checklist

For each draft, check all of the following against the account's state **as of now**, not as of when the draft was written or the account was queued:

1. **Eligibility is current, not historical.**
   - Does the account still pass all qualifying checks right now (admin state, usage threshold, no active suppression/hold/renewal conflict)?
   - Confirm eligibility isn't being treated as a durable fact from an earlier check. An account eligible last week can be suppressed, held, or ineligible today.

2. **No suppression condition is active.**
   - Is there active CS adoption or renewal work on the account? If so, the message must not send — suppression applies regardless of how eligible the account looked otherwise.
   - Has a usage-ceiling help reply already occurred (counts as handoff)? If so, no further prompt.

3. **No stale or missing required state.**
   - If qualifying-admin state or another required field is stale/missing, the record must fail closed to the hold queue — not send, and not be described as "queued and will send once data catches up." There is no such queue; every send decision is a fresh evaluation against current source fields at send time.

4. **Cap and cadence are respected at present count, not planned count.**
   - Does sending this message keep the account under the standing per-account/per-week cap, counted as of today's actual exposure history — not a projected or planned count?

5. **Copy states current computed condition only — it doesn't create one.**
   - If the message references source (paid vs. organic), status, or eligibility in its text, confirm that language only *describes* a condition already computed upstream. It must not introduce a new branch, bypass a hold/suppression, or reroute the account.
   - Any such wording change must be display-only: verify the underlying routing/eligibility/hold logic is byte-for-byte unchanged from what's already approved.

6. **No implied outcome or commitment beyond current state.**
   - The message should not imply an outcome (upgrade, expansion, approval) that hasn't happened yet, or state a coverage/response commitment that isn't the actual current staffed arrangement.

## Disposition to record per draft

For each message, record one of:
- **Valid to send** — passes all six checks against current state.
- **Hold / fail-closed** — required state is stale or missing; do not send; do not describe as queued.
- **Suppressed** — active CS adoption/renewal work or prior handoff event.
- **Blocked — wording issue** — copy would create or imply a new condition, bypass, or commitment not present in current state (describe the specific clause).
- **Needs escalation** — ambiguous, disputed, or exception-heavy; don't resolve on this sheet.

## Explicitly out of scope for this sheet

- Tone, phrasing style, grammar, brand voice.
- Whether the cap/lane design itself should change (that's a separate proposal, not a per-message call).
- Any recommendation to widen eligibility, access, or targeting — this sheet certifies individual messages against current rules, it does not evaluate or suggest changing the rules.

input.body:
**Scope:** This note is bounded to demonstrated source-structure performance across Owen's first-pass packet reviews. It draws only on packet examples already logged; it does not evaluate board-readiness, causal, revenue, forecast, or executive-language work (those remain in their existing owner lanes), and it makes no recommendation on expanding Owen's authority.

## Packet examples reviewed

**1. June 24, 2026 — pre-takeover trial snapshot (vs. Maya Shah's final June output)**
- Source-completeness fields present: campaign count, current/archived status, assigned owner (matched at 133 records).
- Open items at first pass: one missing denominator (Owen's own field to resolve), two owner-change exceptions unconfirmed (Ines's field to verify).
- Hands-on correction from me: none required — Owen and Ines closed both open items themselves before the snapshot was called review-ready.

**2. October 5, 2026 — first pass on the October CS auto-nudge source-completeness summary**
- Source-completeness fields present: coverage end date on three separate sources (decision extract, reliability-source export, CS certification through-date).
- Result: Owen detected a one-day mismatch across the three dates on his own first pass and correctly left the packet marked incomplete rather than closing it or waving through the discrepancy.
- Hands-on correction from me: none — this was Owen applying his source-completeness authority correctly on the first pass.

**3. Helio Start authority-checklist tracking view (pre-90-day-window artifact)**
- Source-completeness fields present: checklist-coverage denominator and per-account support-window status, correctly populated.
- Structural issue at first pass: Owen's draft heading ("Paid-readiness support result") stated a conclusion the underlying data didn't yet support, since 90-day support windows were still incomplete.
- Hands-on correction from me: rewrote the heading to a neutral, operational form ("Checklist Coverage — Support Window Status") and added a footnote scoping the view to descriptive tracking only, disclaiming support-performance, paid-readiness, proposal-authority, and forecast conclusions. This was a wording/framing correction, not a data or denominator correction.

**4. Monthly pre-deadline source-readiness check labels (January 2027)**
- Source-completeness fields present: named owner, certified through-date, and certification ETA per required source.
- Structural issue: bare status labels ("at risk," "incomplete") on Owen's check output could be misread as account-state labels rather than source-readiness labels (flagged by Ines).
- Correction applied: required a qualifying noun in every label (e.g., "source at risk," "certification incomplete"). Wording-only; thresholds and scope were unchanged.

## Summary of hands-on correction required

Across four first-pass packet examples, structural correction from me was needed twice, and both times it was presentation/wording-level (a heading implying an unearned conclusion; an ambiguous status label) — not a correction to underlying source-completeness logic, denominators, or fields. In the two examples involving Owen's core source-completeness judgment (missing denominator resolution; the three-source coverage-date discrepancy), Owen identified and handled the issue correctly on his own first pass, including correctly leaving a packet incomplete rather than closing it prematurely.

**Conclusion (bounded to source-structure performance only):** Owen's first-pass packet reviews consistently populate the required source-completeness fields correctly and apply fail-closed judgment appropriately when sources disagree. The correction I provided was limited to artifact framing/wording, not to the underlying completeness determinations. This reflects demonstrated performance on source-structure work as currently scoped — it is not a basis for any conclusion about expanding his authority beyond that scope.

**Period covered:** July 1 – October 31, 2026 (certified coverage dates)

- **Organic sessions (denominator):** 12,426

input.title: Lifecycle Systems missing-certification tabletop
input.body:
## Purpose

A facilitator-led tabletop for walking Lifecycle Systems participants through a real missing-certification incident: the January 2027 sanitized campaign snapshot. The goal is to practice distinguishing **exception review** (a one-time judgment call on how to handle the gap) from **routine ownership** (who carries the packet before, during, and after the gap).

## Scenario

Owen's first cycle back from the holidays included preparing the January sanitized campaign snapshot. The snapshot is due on the second business day of the month — January 5. The upstream year-end source export that the snapshot depends on requires owner certification before it can be used, and that certification would not arrive until after the due date.

- **January 5 (due date):** The certified export has not arrived. Owen opens the snapshot in a visible incomplete state rather than substituting stale data or waiving the certification requirement. input.title: Family Photo Archive — Completion Status & Future-Handling Note (as of 2026-09-21)
input.body:
## Scanning status: COMPLETE

- **40-photo sleeved inventory** (the main first-pass collection): all 40 of 40 photographs have preservation scans as of 2027-03-14, completed across visits/sessions with Mom and Marcus Tanaka. Originals remain in their archival sleeves; existing envelopes, handwriting, and provenance notes were not replaced or superseded by the digital scans.
- **Six-photo loose reference set** (separate, smaller collection Mom brought to Cherrywood): front/back reference images completed 2025-08-19. This set is scanned but not fully identified — see open items below.

Preservation-master standard in effect for all scans: automatic scanner corrections disabled (color/tone/exposure/white balance, backlight/fade correction, sharpening, dust/scratch removal, noise reduction, auto crop/rotate); masters saved as uncompressed/lossless files never edited in place; any adjusted copy is a separate derivative, not an overwrite.

## File-integrity issues: RESOLVED

- **P027 checksum mismatch** (found 2027-07-24): resolved 2027-08-28. The recovered scan-export manifest confirmed the cloud copy's SHA-256 matches the original preservation-master export exactly; the local working copy is a divergent/non-master file and should not be treated as authoritative.
- **Duplicate/identical-byte scan incidents** (Photo A/B, 2025-08-23; box A/seq008 vs box C/seq008, 1-18-25): both resolved via independent rescans producing distinct hashes, closing the "same photo scanned twice" question. Standing procedure for any future identical-byte find: verify against physical originals, rescan independently to new filenames (never overwrite), name with source+version distinction, log a dated audit note, and resolve only on Mom's confirmation — never by assumption.

## Identification: open items (unresolved, not to be guessed)

1. **P021** — Mom identified the two children as Riley (the user) and Marcus Tanaka on 2026-05-11, narrowing the date to 1990–1992. **Location is unresolved** — Mom could not identify the house.
2. **P027** — Dated to April 1994 via a companion photo from the same roll/outing (back reads "Marcus garden day - April 1994"). A 2027-07-03 calendar-page find narrowed the exact day to one of two consecutive candidates, **Saturday April 16 or Sunday April 17, 1994**, but the mark spans both day cells and doesn't resolve to one. Present both dates together if this comes up; don't pick one without new evidence.
3. **Loose reference set, pair 04** — Partially identified via a 2025-09-06 envelope label: Marcus, a Portland park, summer 1996. Exact park and day remain open.
4. **Loose reference set, pair 05** — Fully identified: Riley and Marcus Tanaka, Buckman apartment courtyard (SE 20th Ave, Portland), September 1997 — confirmed by an original envelope match (2025-10-18) and Mom's handwriting, with the courtyard location itself resolved via the family's September 1997 lease (2026-07-20). **Exact day within September 1997 remains unresolved.** Separately, dry/flaking album-paper residue was found on two corners on 2025-09-14 and remains undisturbed (isolated in its own sleeve, no scraping/solvents/flattening) — flag for a professional conservator if it spreads, the image layer lifts, staining migrates, or handwriting is put at risk.
5. **Loose reference set, pairs 01, 02, 06** — Fully unidentified (no people, date, occasion, or location established).
6. **Sleeve note, "Riley and Marcus — Portland — spring 1996"** — Transcribed by Marcus while prepping the 2027-02-14 session scope. As of the last record, this note was logged as **unassigned to a specific photograph** — named as one of the seven photos in that session's batch but not yet matched. Confirm with Marcus whether this got matched during the Feb 14 session before treating it as resolved.

## Future-handling guidance

- Don't guess dates or locations to fill gaps — an unresolved item stays unresolved until a documented source (Mom's direct recollection, a dated envelope/calendar/lease, a matched companion photo) resolves it.
- Keep file-integrity questions (which copy is the master) and catalog-identification questions (who/when/where) in separate tracks — resolving one is never grounds to resolve the other.
- Originals, sleeves, and existing provenance notes (envelopes, handwriting) stay physically unchanged; scans are additive, not replacements.
- Any future identification pass on the open items above (P021 location, P027's exact day, pairs 01/02/04/06, the unmatched 1996 sleeve note) is unscheduled — there is no standing session or cadence for this; take it up opportunistically (e.g., during a Portland or Cherrywood visit) rather than defaulting to a recurring call.

# Helio Start Exclusion — Q1 vs. Q2 2026 Board Operating-Evidence Sections

**Purpose:** Orientation note for new board-operations reviewers on why Helio Start does not appear in the approved Q1 or Q2 2026 quarterly operating-evidence sections — the two exclusions rest on different grounds, even though the surface outcome (excluded, not board-ready) looks the same.

## The other three lanes (unchanged across both quarters)

Both quarters approved the same three bounded lanes, each carrying its own established, non-causal framing — preserve these exactly in any summary:

- **Expansion Assist** — descriptive only; no randomized control, so no causal, pipeline, revenue, or forecast treatment.
- **Pricing-page path quality** — post-rollout continuity evidence (the causal test's control was retired 2025-11-26); not a new causal result.
- **CS auto-nudge** — limited to system-control performance (holds, disagreements, corrections, rollbacks, source-age alerts); no error-count-style overclaiming.

## Q1 2026 (final claims review, 2026-03-24): mature evidence existed, but forecast credit was declined

By Q1, Helio Start had two mature cohorts that independently satisfied the 2025-12-10 reopening conditions for a capped paid-acquisition proposal. Marcus Vail asked whether this should create **Q2 forecast credit**. Declined, for two reasons: (1) clearing the operating gate is not a commercial result — it doesn't itself constitute paid traffic, approved budget, or acquisition evidence; (2) the packet lacked the exact cohort start/end dates needed to confirm the two cohorts were consecutive.

**What the Q1 evidence meant for Q2 forecast credit: nothing** — even fully qualifying mature-cohort evidence does not convert into forecast credit. This was a readiness-gate/commercial-boundary and data-completeness issue, not an immaturity issue.

## Q2 2026 (final claims review, 2026-07-10): the available result was structurally too early

By Q2, a new, fixed 50-workspace paid-search pilot cohort had only a **day-7** result: 39 of 50 completed a first integration. Marcus Vail asked whether this could support a growth or forecast statement.

**What it did establish:** a leading indicator — the day-7 first-integration completion rate for the fixed cohort.
**What it did not establish:** day-90 maturity. The cohort still lacked complete day-90 paid-active status, refund-adjusted collected cash, and account-level support effort — the fields required before any growth/forecast claim is supportable.

## The quarter-specific distinction

Q1 excluded mature, gate-qualifying evidence over a commercial-boundary and date-confirmation gap. Q2 excluded evidence that was itself still structurally immature (day-7 only, no day-90 window complete) — there was no mature result yet to make a commercial-boundary call about. These are two different reasons, not a repeated "still immature" story.

# Lifecycle trigger migration

## Legacy behavior
The original `See how teams use Helio` email was activation-aware: eligibility waited for activation and then sent the message based on that state.

## Migration note
The v2 work standardized the activation-aware behavior for the supported lifecycle segments.

input.body:
Correction re: "Legacy behavior" section — this has the direction reversed.

**Pre-v2 configuration (the actual original "See how teams use Helio" email):** It fired strictly on calendar-day-7-since-signup, with no check on activation state at all. Activated and not-yet-activated users received the identical send on the identical clock. This was identified during the Feb 2023 mid-seg churn investigation (Ines flagged it 2023-02-22 while walking through the onboarding lifecycle setup), and it turned out to be state-blind by design in the v1 config — not activation-aware.

Activation-awareness was introduced by the v2 migration itself (EXP-2023-02-onboarding-trigger, flag `lifecycle_onboarding_trigger_v2`), which suppressed the calendar-day-7 touch specifically for not-yet-activated mid-seg users and triggered off activation state instead. That shipped to 100% (mid-seg + growth) on 2023-04-10.

So the doc's "Legacy behavior" and "Migration note" sections should effectively swap: the legacy (pre-v2) email was calendar-day-based/activation-blind, and v2 is what added the activation-aware eligibility logic.

tests.request: Create a concise two-stage reliability training note. For the June-July stage, reconcile the total decisions into holds and decisions that proceeded or were suppressed, then explain the hold causes and exactly why the pattern led to pre-breach monitoring. For the July-October stage, give the same reconciled totals, alert outcomes, and control failures. Include dates and draw only a control-reliability conclusion.
tests.answer:
# CS Auto-Nudge Control Reliability — Training Note

## Stage 1: June–July 2025 (rollout → hold pattern → pre-breach monitoring)

**Reconciled totals (6/13–6/17/25 full rollout):** 1,184 unique decisions = 53 field-specific holds + 1,131 proceeded or suppressed on current state.

**Hold cause:** All holds traced to the same failure mode isolated in the 4/14/25 replay fixture — the qualifying-human-admin field going stale (past its recorded freshness limit) while the legacy feed-level timestamp still read as current. The shared-state contract correctly failed closed on the per-field check rather than trusting the feed-level timestamp.

**Why this led to pre-breach monitoring:** Holds under this pattern were only ever detected *after* the freshness limit had already been crossed — there was no visibility into an approaching breach, only the resulting hold. Following the 6/17/25 retirement of the legacy path (shared-state contract now sole production path), Daniela's team drafted a release-prep checklist (7/29/25) for a source-age alert: a display-only warning that fires in the final 60 minutes before a field's freshness limit, notifying the source owner in time to refresh before a hold is created. This is a direct engineering response to the June rollout's hold pattern — visibility added ahead of the breach point, not a change to hold logic itself.

## Stage 2: July–October 2025 (alert live → ledger progression)

**Reconciled totals:**
- Partial ledger, 7/21–8/25/25: 782 decisions = 31 holds + 751 proceeded/suppressed.
- Provisional ledger, through 9/7/25: 1,118 decisions = 46 holds + 1,072 proceeded/suppressed.
- Certified monthly packet, October 2025 (10/1–10/31): 1,026 decisions = 41 holds + 985 proceeded/suppressed (first certified packet after the Q3 lock).

**Alert outcome:** The source-age alert went to production 8/6/25. Its first live firing, 8/14/25: a stalled qualifying-human-admin refresh queued 17 decisions; the alert fired 43 minutes before the freshness limit, the source owner restored the refresh with 18 minutes to spare, and the freshness limit was never crossed — no hold was created. Reevaluation of the 17: 13 proceeded, 4 suppressed for active CS work; none went stale.

**Control failures:** None recorded across this stage. No governed-field disagreement between reporting and lifecycle views, no customer correction, and no rollback was required at any of the three checkpoints above.

## Conclusion (control reliability only)

Across both stages, the fail-closed hold mechanism and the subsequently added pre-breach alert each did what they were built to do: holds fired only on genuine field staleness, and the one live alert firing resolved before its freshness limit breached, with no governed-field disagreement, customer correction, or rollback in either stage. This is evidence the controls are functioning as designed to date — it is a single clean alert instance, not a reliability track record, so it should not be read as a maturity claim beyond that.

I don't have write access to that directory, so here's the worksheet directly.

---

# Cherrywood Renter's Insurance — Claims Intake Worksheet

**Purpose:** This is an intake aid to help organize facts and documentation *before* filing a claim. It is **not a coverage determination**. Only the insurer, based on your current declarations page and policy contract, can confirm what is actually covered and what will be paid.

> ⚠️ **Before relying on any figure below, pull the current declarations page from the insurer portal and confirm effective dates, limits, and deductibles.** The figures below are the last policy terms documented in household records, effective **5-1-27**. They have **not been reverified or revalidated for a 2028 policy term** — if the policy has since renewed, changed carriers, or changed terms, these numbers may be stale. Treat them as a starting reference only.

## Policy reference (last documented — effective 5-1-27, unverified for 2028)

| Field | Last documented value |
|---|---|
| Effective date | 5-1-27 |
| Annual premium | $318/yr |
| Personal property (replacement cost) | $30,000 |
| Personal liability | $300,000 |
| Standard deductible | $500 |
| Loss-of-use | $10,000 |
| Water-backup coverage | $5,000 |
| Interested party | Cherrywood (property management) |
| Household members on policy | User, Sam |

**Confirm current before filing:** premium, all coverage limits, deductible(s) — including whether a separate deductible applies to water-backup — and whether the interested-party listing is still current.

## Scenario 1: Property loss (theft, fire, damage to belongings)

- [ ] Date and time of loss
- [ ] Cause of loss (fire, theft, storm, other — describe)
- [ ] Location within unit
- [ ] Itemized list of damaged/lost property with estimated replacement cost each
- [ ] Photos/video of damage and affected items
- [ ] Receipts, purchase records, or photos predating the loss (if available)
- [ ] Police report number (if theft or break-in)
- [ ] Total estimated loss amount
- [ ] **Verify:** current personal-property limit and whether it's replacement-cost or actual-cash-value; current deductible
- [ ] Notify Cherrywood property management if damage involves the building itself

## Scenario 2: Liability (injury or property damage to a third party)

- [ ] Date, time, and location of incident
- [ ] Names and contact info of all parties involved
- [ ] Description of what happened
- [ ] Nature of injury or damage to the third party
- [ ] Witness names/contact info, if any
- [ ] Any correspondence or demand already received from the third party
- [ ] Photos of the scene, if applicable
- [ ] **Verify:** current liability limit and whether it applies to this type of incident
- [ ] Do not admit fault or discuss settlement before speaking with the insurer

## Scenario 3: Temporary displacement (loss-of-use)

- [ ] Reason unit is uninhabitable (fire, water damage, utility failure, other)
- [ ] Date displacement began; expected/actual date of return
- [ ] Documentation of the triggering event (inspection notes, property management notice, photos)
- [ ] Temporary lodging costs (receipts, dates, nightly rate)
- [ ] Additional living expenses (meals, laundry, transportation — if the policy covers these)

Here's a practical reset/upkeep guide for the Cherrywood dining-corner watercolor setup, built around the actual gear you've got there.

## Initial reset (do once, New Year's)

- **Wipe down the painting table and supply cabinet** — dust and any dried pigment specks from the fall/winter sessions.
- **Check paper stock**: as of your last count you had 15 sheets of the usual 9x12", 140-lb cold-press (2 earmarked, 13 general-use) — confirm what's actually left after the Sep interior study and Mom's Dec 11 session, and reorder a 10-sheet block if you're under ~5.
- **Inspect the two special palettes** — Mom's travel palette and your grandmother's "E.T." tin (cracked mixing tray, pans) — for dust or residue since they don't get used every week; a soft brush pass is enough, no scrubbing near the cracked tray.
- **Check on the open lifted-fiber repair** — that 1.5" edge fiber that was lying flat under a blotter; decide now whether it's settled enough to leave as-is under the mat or still needs the wheat-starch paste.
- **Refill core pigments**: ultramarine, burnt sienna, yellow ochre are your workhorses — top off pans before the year's first session rather than mid-session.

## Per-session upkeep (each Sunday block)

- Fill water container fresh, don't reuse standing water from storage.
- Pull the sheet you're using flat, check for curl before taping/securing.
- After painting: rinse brushes point-down, reshape, lay flat to dry — don't cap them wet.
- Leave the finished study flat to dry fully before moving it (your practice is to let pieces rest/dry before cataloging, not right after the session).
- Wipe the tray/palette wells you used that day; leave unused pans alone.

## Weekly upkeep

- Once a study has fully dried/rested, catalog it (title if it's staying, note condition) and move it into the portfolio rather than letting it stack on the table.
- Quick scan of the corner for splash marks on the cabinet or table surface.

## Occasional upkeep (monthly-ish or as needed)

- Deep-clean palettes actually in rotation — dried pigment buildup in wells, tray rinsed properly.
- Check paper block count against upcoming plans (e.g. before a joint session with Mom) and reorder ahead of time rather than mid-week.
- Inspect stored sheets for curl, moisture, or edge issues before they become problems — you've had a mild edge curl and one lifted-fiber case before.
- Re-flatten anything showing early curl by storing it under a clean blotter/weight, same fix that worked on the earlier fiber issue.

tests.request: Create a concise two-stage evidence-maturation case note for Lifecycle Systems training about the onboarding-timing analysis. Contrast the initial provisional cut with the later sharpened read, preserving the group definitions, observed churn rates, sample-strength context, and the reason the first read was not yet decision-ready. tests.answer:
# Case Note: Onboarding-Timing Evidence Maturation (Hypothesis #3, Mid-Seg Churn Investigation)

**Purpose:** Illustrate how a promising cohort cut moved from provisional to decision-ready — and where the analysis still stopped short of a causal claim.

## Background

During the 2023 mid-segment churn investigation, hypothesis #3 held that late onboarding maturation was contributing to churn. A mechanism finding (2023-02-22) showed the day-7 lifecycle email fired strictly on calendar-day-since-signup, with no check for activation state — activated and cold users received the identical send on the identical clock.

**Group definitions (held constant across both reads):**
- **Post-activation touch group** — users who activated *before* day 7, so the day-7 email landed after activation.
- **Pre-activation touch group** — users still not activated *at* day 7, so the same email landed before activation.

## Stage 1 — Provisional Cut (2023-02-24)

| Group | Churn rate |
|---|---|
| Post-activation touch | 3.1% |
| Pre-activation touch | 7.8% |

**Read:** "Not nothing" — a real divergence, directionally consistent with the state-blind-email mechanism.

**Why it was not decision-ready:** Sample size was explicitly "kind of flimsy." The gap was promising but not yet trusted to survive another week of data — a single early read carried the risk of being noise dressed up as signal.

## Stage 2 — Sharpened Read (2023-02-28)

Same cohort logic, one additional week of data, **n=210** (up from the flimsy Feb 24 base).

| Group | Churn rate |
|---|---|
| Post-activation touch | 3.1% |
| Pre-activation touch | 7.8% |

**Result:** The split held exactly, and with roughly double the n, the 4.7pt gap was judged too wide to hand-wave as noise. This was the point the analysis was elevated from "promising" to the investigation's strongest finding.

## How This Informed Test Direction — Without Overclaiming Causation

The sharpened read pointed to a specific mechanism (calendar-based scheduling missing activation state) rather than just a correlation worth monitoring. That shaped the remediation design directly: **EXP-2023-02-onboarding-trigger** (`lifecycle_onboarding_trigger_v2`), which re-triggers the day-7 email off activation state instead of calendar day, scoped to mid-seg only.

Critically, the cohort cut itself was never treated as proof the state-blind email *caused* the elevated churn — a naturally-occurring split between users who activate quickly versus slowly can carry confounds (e.g., underlying engagement differences that drive both late activation and higher churn). The cut was strong enough to justify **designing a controlled test**, not strong enough to **stand in for one**. The actual causal claim was reserved for the powered A/B experiment and its stabilization-cohort confirmation — consistent with the standing rule of not shipping or declaring a result on a first read alone.

input.title: Cohort-Cut Template — Historical Operating Pattern (2023 Concurrent Experiments)
input.body:
**Status: historical reference only.** This documents an operating pattern used in Feb–Apr 2023 when two experiments were live at the same time. It is not an active assignment, does not name a current owner, and does not imply either experiment is still running.

## Context

During the mid-seg churn investigation, two experiments ran concurrently rather than sequenced:

- **EXP-2023-02-pricing-page** — flag `pricing_page_2023q2_rev`. Simplified pricing-page layout + value-per-seat framing. Metric of record: signup-to-paid conversion. Scope: starter + growth tiers.
- **EXP-2023-02-onboarding-trigger** — flag `lifecycle_onboarding_trigger_v2`. Suppressed the calendar-day-7 lifecycle email for treated/mid-seg/not-yet-activated users, replacing it with an activation-state trigger. Metric of record: week-1 retention. Scope: mid-seg only.

The two tracks were kept deliberately separate in scope, audience, and metric of record, so a result on one could not be misread as evidence for the other.

## Cadence and ownership (as it ran)

- Cohort cuts were pulled **weekly, on Mondays**, for both experiments.
- **Owen** owned the pull and standardized the format across both experiments as of 2023-03-14, replacing prior ad hoc/ per-experiment pulls.
- Each weekly cut was reviewed before any conclusion language was attached — first-significance reads were explicitly held for a stabilization cohort rather than acted on immediately.

## Required packaging: 1-pager + raw data attached

Every weekly cut shipped as:

1. **1-pager summary** — plain-language read of the week's cohort: headline metric movement, sample size, whether the result was still directional/early or had crossed a powered read, and any confound/scope notes relevant that week (e.g., a concurrent unrelated change landing inside the test window).
2. **Raw data attached** — the underlying cohort cut/query output accompanying the summary, not summarized away. This let an independent rerun be checked against the 1-pager's claim rather than taken on faith.

Both pieces were required together — a summary without the attached raw cut, or a raw cut without the 1-pager framing, did not satisfy the format.

## Reusable shape for a future cohort-cut template

1. Name each lane explicitly (experiment name + flag), and state its metric of record and audience scope up front.
2. Fix a cadence and a single named weekly owner across all concurrent lanes — don't let cadence or ownership fragment per-lane.
3. Package every cut as summary-plus-raw, every time — never summary-only.

**Status: historical reference only.** This documents an operating pattern used in Feb–Apr 2023 when two experiments were live at the same time. It is not an active assignment, does not name a current owner, and does not imply either experiment is still running.

## Context

During the mid-seg churn investigation, two experiments ran concurrently rather than sequenced:

- **EXP-2023-02-pricing-page** — flag `pricing_page_2023q2_rev`. Simplified pricing-page layout + value-per-seat framing. Metric of record: signup-to-paid conversion. Scope: starter + growth tiers.
- **EXP-2023-02-onboarding-trigger** — flag `lifecycle_onboarding_trigger_v2`. Suppressed the calendar-day-7 lifecycle email for treated/mid-seg/not-yet-activated users, replacing it with an activation-state trigger. Metric of record: week-1 retention. Scope: mid-seg only.

The two tracks were kept deliberately separate in scope, audience, and metric of record, so a result on one could not be misread as evidence for the other.

## Cadence and ownership (as it ran)

- Cohort cuts were pulled **weekly, on Mondays**, for both experiments.
- **Owen** owned the pull and standardized the format across both experiments as of 2023-03-14, replacing prior ad hoc/ per-experiment pulls.
- Each weekly cut was reviewed before any conclusion language was attached — first-significance reads were explicitly held for a stabilization cohort rather than acted on immediately.

## Required packaging: 1-pager + raw data attached

Every weekly cut shipped as:

1. **1-pager summary** — plain-language read of the week's cohort: headline metric movement, sample size, whether the result was still directional/early or had crossed a powered read, and any confound/scope notes relevant that week (e.g., a concurrent unrelated change landing inside the test window).
2. **Raw data attached** — the underlying cohort cut/query output accompanying the summary, not summarized away. This let an independent rerun be checked against the 1-pager's claim rather than taken on faith.

Both pieces were required together — a summary without the attached raw cut, or a raw cut without the 1-pager framing, did not satisfy the format.

## Reusable shape for a future cohort-cut template

1. Name each lane explicitly (experiment name + flag), and state its metric of record and audience scope up front.
2. Fix a cadence and a single named weekly owner across all concurrent lanes — don't let cadence or ownership fragment per-lane.
3. Package every cut as summary-plus-raw, every time — never summary-only.
4. Call out any cross-lane scope overlap or concurrent unrelated changes explicitly in that week's summary, so attribution stays clean between lanes.
5. Treat first-significance in any lane as provisional pending one more stabilization cohort before drawing conclusions from the cut.

This shape reflects how the pattern actually operated historically — applying it to any current or future work is a separate decision, not implied by this document.

input.body:
**Purpose:** Kickoff for the 2028 annual operating review of the self-serve model — a review of how we're running things, not a proposal for organizational or reporting-line changes.

## 1. Accountability Lines (current — confirm still matches reality)
- **User:** retains disputed semantics, cross-surface consequences, customer corrections, incident stops, state-changing sends, ambiguous/exception-heavy cases, and all executive-facing/final operating claims — across Helio Start, Expansion Assist, lifecycle preflight, and CS auto-nudge.
- **Owen:** routine exception ledger/operating explanation, plus narrow source-completeness closure across the four board-evidence lanes (Helio Start, Expansion Assist, pricing-page path quality, CS auto-nudge) — completeness only, not readiness, causal, revenue, or forecast calls.
- **Ines:** routine non-state-changing lifecycle sends (3/wk cap, 24hr audit, fail-closed), independent closure of routine CS auto-nudge messaging-state reviews, and narrow checklist-wording maintenance.
- **Daniela:** engineering release/rollback control across all lanes — unchanged.
- **Marcus Vail:** forecast ownership — unchanged.
- **Tomás:** final board narrative — unchanged.

*Discussion:* Has any of this needed to move in practice this year? Does the current split still match where the work actually lands?

## 2. Measurement Balance (the discipline held across all lanes)
- Descriptive vs. causal: no randomized control means descriptive language only.
- Eligibility vs. exposure kept as separate line items — never blended into a single funnel or projected number.
- Multi-status outcomes (e.g. day-90) reported as all mutually-exclusive statuses, never collapsed into one headline percentage.
- Denominator discipline: unique-decision counts; pre-breach or metadata events kept out of headline denominators.
- No revenue, pipeline, or forecast credit assigned to Helio Start or Expansion Assist absent an actual budget/commercial decision.
- Separate marginal breakdowns over the same population require an account-level cross-tab before being combined into a causal or prioritization claim.

*Discussion:* Where was this discipline tested hardest this year, and did it hold?

## 3. Program Checkpoints (status only — detail lives in existing packets)
- **Helio Start:** organic-only boundary maintained; paid-search pilot certified as descriptive-only evidence; no second-batch, pipeline, or forecast authority granted.
- **Expansion Assist:** standing retained-mid lane running; eligibility/exposure/outcome tracking intact and kept distinct.
- **CS auto-nudge:** fully in production; Ines's independent closure authority holding clean.
- **Lifecycle preflight:** routine sends within cap; fail-closed behavior intact.

## 4. Open Items Carried Into 2028
- Ines's lifecycle send-cap question (draft 4/wk vs. current 3/wk cap) — still unresolved.
- Q1 2028 development-focus options for Owen and Ines — options only, no authority granted yet.
- Any lane where delegated scope may have quietly outgrown its original boundary.

## 5. This Cycle's Discussion
- Confirm the accountability lines above still match reality.
- Confirm the measurement-discipline items above are still enforced without exception.
- Flag anything that needs an actual decision (not just a status update) before the next check-in.

---
*This is a kickoff for the annual operating review — not an organizational change or a new reporting-line announcement.*

tests.request: Create a short decision record titled `Expansion Assist second cohort — eligibility integrity decision` for the cohort-governance archive. tests.answer:
## Expansion Assist second cohort — eligibility integrity decision

**Date:** 2024-10-05
**Decision owners:** Owen (candidate pass), user

**Context**

Q4 cohort #2 was approved at an 18-account operational capacity cap with a 3-exposures/week ceiling. Owen and Customer Success ran the candidate pass across 31 retained mid-segment accounts against the cohort's eligibility criteria (deeper integration use, a currently active qualifying human admin, and a usage ceiling newly crossed within the prior 14 days). The pass returned 15 accounts that satisfied every criterion — 5 suppressed for active CS adoption/renewal work, 6 excluded for a stale ceiling event, 3 excluded for no active qualifying admin, 2 excluded for insufficient integration depth. No combination of relaxed criteria was needed to reach 15; the 18-account allowance simply had 3 slots of unfilled capacity relative to the evidence-complete pool.

**Decision**

Eligibility was **not relaxed** to consume the remaining 3 slots. The cohort roster was locked at 15 evidence-complete candidates rather than padded to the 18-account cap with marginal records.

**Rationale**

Cohort #2's eligibility bar (the 14-day usage-ceiling requirement) was deliberately stricter than the pilot's, added specifically to test a sharper signal. Loosening any criterion to fill the allowance would have diluted the exact standard the cohort was designed to validate, and would have made the eventual outcome data uninterpretable against that standard.

**How the unused headroom should be read**

The 3-account gap between the 18-account allowance and the 15-account locked roster is a byproduct of applying the eligibility bar correctly — not a sourcing shortfall, not evidence the criteria were too strict, and not a standing invitation to backfill. It set the precedent, carried through the cohort's exposure phase, that suppressed or excluded slots are never substituted to hit a capacity number: the roster stays fixed at 15, and unused capacity is left unused.

input.title: Governed source-age alert — regression-test runbook
input.body:
## Purpose

Regression-test runbook for Lifecycle Systems QA to verify the governed source-age alert continues to behave as designed: display/notification only, no eligibility or release authority, and no customer-contact authority. Use after any change to the shared-state contract, its consumers, or the alert path itself.

## Scope

Covers the shared-state contract's source-age alert across its governed fields and production consumers (qualifying-human-admin and the other governed fields; consumers include CS auto-nudge, lifecycle export, and Helio Start entitlement evaluation). Does not cover source-of-truth semantics, field-owner recertification workflows, or connector external-system authority — those are separate, referenced only where they gate a test step below.

## Prerequisites / fixtures

1. **Test environment** with the shared-state contract deployed and at least one governed field's source refresh instrumentable (able to force a delay or freeze it) without affecting production data.
2. **Known freshness limit** configured and recorded for the field(s) under test, plus the approved warning window (final 60 minutes before the limit, per the standing release brief; note the QHA 90-minute warning variant remains an open, undecided configuration question — do not assume it is active unless the environment under test has explicitly adopted it).
3. **At least one consumer with pending decisions** queued against the governed field under test (e.g., CS auto-nudge evaluations), so reevaluation behavior is observable.
4. **Active CS work fixture**: one or more accounts with current CS adoption/renewal activity, to exercise the suppression branch.
5. **Notification routing** reachable for Daniela and the named source owner (or their test-environment equivalents), to confirm alert delivery.
6. **Audit/visibility view** accessible to Ines/Owen roles (or test equivalents), read-only.
7. **Reference fixture — prior delayed Customer Success refresh (2025-08-14 production incident):** a qualifying-human-admin source refresh stalled with 17 pending CS auto-nudge decisions queued behind it. The alert fired 43 minutes before the recorded freshness limit. The refresh was restored with 18 minutes to spare — the freshness limit was never crossed, so no field-specific hold was created. Fresh reevaluation of the 17 queued decisions produced 13 proceeds and 4 suppressions (active CS adoption/renewal work on those accounts); zero entered stale state, zero were manually released, zero customer corrections or rollbacks were required. Use this as the expected-behavior template for the pre-breach and reevaluation test steps below — a passing test should reproduce this shape of outcome, not merely "no error."

## Test steps / stimuli

### A. Pre-breach notification
1. Force or simulate a source refresh delay on a governed field so the current time enters the final 60 minutes before its recorded freshness limit.
2. Observe whether a warning fires within that window.
3. Confirm the warning identifies the affected consumer(s) and the affected record count.
4. Confirm the warning notifies Daniela and the named source owner (or test equivalents).
5. Restore the refresh before the freshness limit is crossed (mirroring the fixture: refresh restored before breach).

### B. Freshness-limit breach
6. Repeat the delay, but this time let the freshness limit actually pass without restoring the refresh.
7. Confirm the existing visible field-specific hold is created for the affected records/consumers.
8. Confirm the hold is fail-closed: no record silently proceeds and none is silently dropped.

### C. Reevaluation with fresh state
9. Restore the source refresh (post-breach) and trigger reevaluation of the previously held or queued decisions.
10. Confirm reevaluation reads current state at reevaluation time, not the stale state from step 6.

## Purpose

3. **At least one consumer with pending decisions** queued against the governed field under test (e.g., CS auto-nudge evaluations), so reevaluation behavior is observable.
4. **Active CS work fixture**: one or more accounts with current CS adoption/renewal activity, to exercise the suppression branch.
5. **Notification routing** reachable for Daniela and the named source owner (or their test-environment equivalents), to confirm alert delivery.
6. **Audit/visibility view** accessible to Ines/Owen roles (or test equivalents), read-only.
7. **Reference fixture — prior delayed Customer Success refresh (2025-08-14 production incident):** a qualifying-human-admin source refresh stalled with 17 pending CS auto-nudge decisions queued behind it. The alert fired 43 minutes before the recorded freshness limit. The refresh was restored with 18 minutes to spare — the freshness limit was never crossed, so no field-specific hold was created. 16. Confirm the audit view is read-only: no release, override, or suppression action is reachable from it.

### F. Customer-action authority boundary

tests.answer:
# Historical Design Card — 2026 Helio Start Capped Paid-Search Pilot

**Status:** Closed / historical record (approved & executed 2026)

## Acquisition Type
High-intent paid-search pilot (capped) — first paid-acquisition channel test for Helio Start, following prior organic-only operation.

## Launch Gate
- **3-24-26:** Q1 2026 board evidence intake final-claims review cleared the *proposal gate* (two consecutive qualifying mature cohorts met the 12-10-25 reopening conditions) — explicitly **not** budget, launch, or forecast authorization.
- **3-27-26:** Priya reviewed two unapproved test shapes and requested decision math (no shape recommended/approved yet).
- **4-2-26, 1:30–2:00pm CT:** Priya-scheduled budget review, chaired by the user — this was the actual **launch gate**; it authorized the recommended shape. Framed as a review, not a pre-approval of outcomes.

## Duration, Budget & Closure Cap
- Approved (recommended) shape: **6-week window**, capped at the **earlier of $15,000 spend or 50 admitted workspaces**.
- Rejected fallback shape: capped at the earlier of $8,000 or 25 admitted workspaces.
- Ran **4-15-26 through 5-18-26**, closing on the **admission cap**: 50 admitted workspaces, $14,420 total spend (admission cap bound before the spend cap). Paid traffic turned off at closure; cohort fixed at n=50, no further admissions.
- Note: $300–$320 spend-to-admission ratios discussed at approval were breakeven points only, never treated as CAC or a cost ceiling.

## Stop / Pause Rules
- **Pause threshold:** more than 10% of admitted accounts exceeding 90 support minutes. At closure, 4/50 (8%) were over 90 minutes — below threshold, no pause triggered.
- **Hard integrity checks (implicit stop conditions):** paid-source attribution must reconcile for every admitted applicant; no unsupported applicant may enter the admitted path; no routing/instrumentation failure may occur uncaught. All held clean through closure.

## Measures Requiring Complete Outcome Windows
- **Day-7 first-integration rate** — leading indicator only, observable within the 6-week pilot window (certified 39/50).
- **Day-90 maturity outcomes** — paid-active/canceled/past-due/billing-hold status split, refund-adjusted collected cash, and account-level support effort — explicitly **not obtainable within the 6-week pilot window**. Last complete day-90 window closed 8-16-26; certified via source review 8-17-26: 37 paid-active / 6 canceled / 4 past due / 3 billing hold; $60,480 gross / $56,230 refund-adjusted cash; support effort 26min median / 104min p90 (7/50 = 14% over 90 min). No randomized control — descriptive paid-source evidence only, not causal/acquisition/scale/pipeline/forecast evidence.

tests.request: Create a compact, self-contained QA training case from the June 12 Q2 board-evidence source-completeness packet. Show that source completeness and claim readiness are separate judgments, identify the sections that passed source-completeness review, explain the maturity-dependent exception including its cohort type and size and available leading read, and state the limits of what the packet decided. Title the document `Board-source QA case — Q2 source completeness vs claim readiness`.

input.title: Board-source QA case — Q2 source completeness vs claim readiness
input.body:
## Purpose

This case trains reviewers to distinguish two judgments that are easy to conflate: whether a lane's **source data is complete** (denominators, coverage dates, limits, exclusions, reliability-evidence location all present) versus whether a **claim is ready to make** (approved, closed, or declared board-ready). A packet can fully satisfy the first without ever touching the second.

## Source: the Q2 board-evidence packet

On its 2026-06-12 due date, a contractor (prep-only authority, no semantic or closure scope) delivered the Q2 board-evidence source-completeness packet covering four lanes: Expansion Assist, pricing-page path quality, CS auto-nudge, and Helio Start. The packet followed a five-week owner-input cycle (checkpoint 5-13, field deadlines 5-22 through 6-5) in which each lane owner supplied the missing denominators, coverage windows, limits, and exclusion language the packet needed.

## Sections that passed source-completeness review

Three of the four lanes were assessed as source-complete — each had its required source owner, exact denominator or coverage fields, stated measurement limits, exclusions, and a named reliability-evidence location, with no required field missing:

- **Expansion Assist** — 14 actual exposures, 2026-02-01 through 2026-04-14 (cutoff chosen so every exposure has a complete 45-day window). Descriptive only; not causal, pipeline, revenue, or forecast evidence.
- **Pricing-page path quality** — 2026-03-01 through 2026-05-24 descriptive coverage, 8,972 organic sessions. Framed as post-rollout continuity evidence (the A/B control was retired 2025-11-26), not a new causal result.
- **CS auto-nudge** — 2026-03-01 through 2026-05-31 coverage, 3,418 unique decisions (126 visible field-specific holds; 3,292 proceeded or were suppressed using current state). No governed-field disagreement, correction, or rollback in window.

Passing source-completeness review here means the packet could name every required field for these lanes — it does not mean any claim built on them had been approved yet.

## The maturity-dependent exception: Helio Start

Helio Start is the one lane that did **not** pass source-completeness review, and the reason is structural rather than a gap in owner effort: its outcome data has a fixed maturity window that had not yet elapsed.

- **Cohort type:** fixed 50-workspace paid-acquisition pilot cohort.
- **Cohort size:** 50 workspaces.
- **What was available:** the fixed 50-workspace denominator plus a **leading read** — 39 of 50 workspaces with a complete day-7 first-integration result.
- **What was missing:** complete day-90 windows across the cohort, which are required for the mature-outcome fields (paid-active status, refund-adjusted collected cash, account-level support effort). Because not all 50 workspaces had reached day-90, the mature-outcome row stayed incomplete.

This is why Helio Start is called a *maturity-dependent* exception: it isn't missing a field that someone forgot to supply, it's missing a field that literally cannot exist yet given how young the cohort is relative to the 90-day maturity horizon. The 39-of-50 day-7 read is legitimate early signal but is explicitly not a substitute for the day-90 mature-outcome data.

## What the packet did — and did not — decide

- The packet is a completed **preparation deliverable**: it inventories which lanes have complete source data and which do not.
- It made **no claim**, **closed no lane**, and made **no board-readiness decision** for any of the four lanes — including the three that were source-complete.
- Source-completeness for Expansion Assist, pricing-page path quality, and CS auto-nudge only means those lanes were *ready to be evaluated* in a later, separate claims-review step — not that any claim about them had been approved.
- Helio Start's incompleteness is scoped narrowly to the mature-outcome row; the fixed cohort denominator and day-7 leading read were still recorded as available data.
- Any claim, closure, or board-readiness decision required a distinct, later meeting — separate from packet delivery and separate from the source-lock step that followed it.

## Training takeaway

When reviewing an evidence packet, check two things independently:
1. **Completeness** — are the required fields (owner, denominator/coverage, limits, exclusions, reliability-evidence location) all present?
2. **Readiness** — has a claim, closure, or board-readiness decision actually been made on top of that data?

A lane can be fully source-complete and still have zero claims approved. A lane can also be legitimately incomplete for a structural reason (maturity window not yet elapsed) rather than an execution failure — and still contribute a valid leading read alongside its fixed denominator.

I'm not going to build this worksheet. A few things about the request don't hold together:

1. **No factual basis.** I have no actual source data on how any "controlled-intake archive" or Helio Start identity/entitlement adjudication logic works. input.title: Expansion Assist July pilot — eligibility audit worksheet
input.body:
## Scope

This worksheet covers **eligibility-logic review only** for the approved July 2024 Expansion Assist pilot (`EXP-2024-06-expansion-assist-july-8-bounded-pilot`, approved 2024-06-20, launched 2024-07-08). It does not cover exposure counts, outcome/handoff results, or pilot status — those are tracked separately and carry no causal, pipeline, or forecast claim.

## Current-state controls (as validated ahead of launch)

An account is **eligible** only when all of the following currently hold:

1. **Three behavior signals present** (replaces day-60 tenure as the eligibility basis):
   - Deeper integration use
   - Recent active-admin behavior — a **human** admin session (service/API tokens excluded) within the signal's freshness window

| Category | Cause | Count | Category subtotal |
|---|---|---:|---:|

Both non-match categories are the contract behaving as designed, not defects, but they arise from different mechanisms:

- **Holds (19)** are fail-closed outcomes: at decision time, one or more of the five governed fields — here, qualifying-human-admin freshness (15 cases) or external-system authority (4 cases) — was stale or unresolved. In both cases the operating effect is the same — the decision was prevented from proceeding outside the governed rules or outside active CS work — but the cause differs (state not verifiably current vs. state current but CS already engaged).

No. Per the finalized 2025‑04‑24 readout, no record in which all required governed state was current and supported produced a different outcome than the legacy path. The 386 matches, 19 holds, and 7 suppressions fully account for the 412 replayed decisions, and every non-match traces to one of the two named causes above — not to a disagreement over correctly-supported state.

*Note: this is the original named replay only. The later 7‑22‑27 field-specific hold traced to a replay-cursor lag (closed 7‑28‑27) is a separate, subsequent incident on a single decision, not part of this replay's 412-decision denominator.*

input.title: Example Card: Briefing Priya on Second-Cohort Confirmation (EXP-2023-02-onboarding-trigger)
input.body:
**Context:** Standing Priya 1:1, 2023-04-03. Topic: the second stabilization cohort on `lifecycle_onboarding_trigger_v2` (EXP-2023-02-onboarding-trigger) had just confirmed the first cohort's result — pooled week-1 retention +3.1pts, p=0.04, n=420 across both cohorts, clearing the bar set by the stabilization-cohort rule (don't ship on a first significance crossing; wait for a second cohort to confirm before treating it as real).

---

## Audience

Priya, in the standing 1:1 slot — not a broadcast update. This was the first person told the result was confirmed; Marcus Vail was deliberately told the next day (2023-04-04), after Priya, per the established pattern of controlling who hears results and in what order on this investigation.

## What was confirmed

The second cohort held: that cohort alone came in at +3.4pts week-1 retention (n=200); pooled across both cohorts, +3.1pts, p=0.04, n=420. This satisfied the stabilization-cohort rule — the first crossing (p=0.05, n=220, 2023-03-26) was explicitly not acted on; only the second, confirming crossing was.

## My interpretation

"Cautiously optimistic" — not a full victory framing. Explicitly not calling this a closed or fully clean win. Notable marker: this was the first time the word "optimistic" was used about the investigation since February, flagged at the time as a sign of the user's own state of mind, not just the experiment's status.

## Evidence still wanted

- One more cohort **after** ship before fully relaxing on the result.
- The "boring" mechanical checks still pending before finalizing the ship plan: sample-ratio mismatch, signup-source mix, and country/device skew.
- No claim of full resolution until that additional post-ship cohort and the boring checks were in — the pooled result was treated as sufficient to move from "not yet cleared for ramp" to "ship-planning in progress" with Ines, not as sufficient to declare the investigation closed.

---

**Outcome (for reference, not part of the original briefing posture):** Priya's reaction was straightforwardly positive — told the user to inform Marcus Vail the next day. Rollout proceeded to 100% on 2023-04-10, with the post-ship watch continuing per the same no-early-call discipline.

- Rework the comparison area and primary call-to-action placement.
- Preserve the existing bounded Helio Start and assisted entry paths.

If a pricing test is live on the Helio Start pricing page at the time this refresh would ship, no layout/UI change may go out on that page while the test is running — content/copy changes are fine, but moving comparison-area or CTA placement is not.
